assumptions: The rule given is the real acceptance criterion for every row.
limits: Asserts the same thing of every row; a cross-row comparison needs summarize_rows first.
bio.jane/contract.noScientificClaim: Applies a rule to each row and stops the run; the science is in whatever produced the table.
bio.jane/contract.question: Does every row of this table satisfy the rule, and which rows broke it?

description: A QC gate over a TABLE: assert something about every row at once (every band inside a size window, no guide above an off-target score, at least three assays under a penalty). Fails the pipeline (so everything downstream skips) and names the rows that broke the rule.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

count.description: N, for the counted requirements. Only applies when require is at_least or at_most or exactly.

field.description: which field of each row to test (e.g. `size`, `score`). Leave empty when the rows are plain numbers.

items.description: the rows to check. Wire a json/list output (bands, guides, assays, amplicons).

label.description: what this gate is checking, in your words. It becomes the message when it fails.

max.description: upper bound, inclusive. Only applies when operator is between.

min.description: lower bound, inclusive. Only applies when operator is between.

operator.description: how each row is compared. Values: == (equals), != (does not equal), > (greater than), >= (at least), < (less than), <= (at most), between (between (inclusive)), in (is one of), not_in (is none of), contains (contains text), is_true (is true), not_empty (is not empty).

record.description: optional: the record this gate is guarding. It comes back out of `record` when the check passes, so the gate sits in the middle of a chain.

report_only.description: report the verdict instead of stopping the run: wire `passed` (or `failed`) into another step's condition to choose a branch.

require.description: what must hold across the table. Values: all (every row), any (at least one row), none (no row), at_least (at least N rows), at_most (at most N rows), exactly (exactly N rows).

set.description: the values the field must be one of (or none of). Only applies when operator is in or not_in.

text.description: the text the field must contain. Only applies when operator is contains.

value.description: the value to compare against. Only applies when operator is == or != or > or >= or < or <=.

name: check_rows

failed.description: the opposite verdict, so the ELSE arm of a branch needs no extra step. Only meaningful with `report_only` on

matched.description: how many rows met the per-row condition

offenders.description: the rows that did NOT meet it: what to look at when the gate fails

passed.description: whether the requirement held. As a gate this is true whenever it is read downstream; with `report_only` on it is the real verdict, for driving a branch

record.description: the guarded record, unchanged. Wire it into the next node's $subject to make that step conditional
